projects.title: ShadowTrace
projects.logline: What was said is only the surface. ShadowTrace reads a WhatsApp chat like a detective — patterns, people, moods and moments — then lets you ask it anything.
build: Built a conversation-intelligence platform in Python (~10K lines) that processes 1M+ messages into interactive analytics with Streamlit and Plotly.
Designed a RAG pipeline with LangChain and FAISS for semantic search and grounded Q&A, with embeddings that fall back from Gemini to OpenRouter to a local model.
Engineered a multi-provider LLM router (Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter, Mistral) with per-provider cooldowns and truncation detection, keeping AI features available when a provider hits its quota.
Implemented 6+ NLP modules — VADER sentiment, emotion and intent detection, LDA/BERTopic topic modeling, YAKE/KeyBERT keywords, toxicity scoring and Hinglish language detection.
Answered factual questions ("who talks the most?") deterministically from computed analytics, skipping the LLM entirely for speed, cost and accuracy.
Optimised performance with lazy section loading and multi-layer caching of parsing, NLP results, RAG indexes and exports.
features: Ask the chat anything — RAG Q&A over your messages with conversational memory
Grounded AI: stats are computed in Python first, so the LLM narrates facts, never invents them
4-provider LLM fallback (Gemini → Groq → OpenRouter → Mistral) with automatic cooldowns
Semantic search that finds messages by meaning, not keywords (FAISS vector index)
Sentiment, emotion, topics and toxicity — tuned for Hinglish and informal text
AI summaries, highlights, people analysis and a conversation quality score

projects.title: MediRAG
projects.logline: Meet Dr. Insight — a medical assistant that answers only from trusted sources, spots emergencies before the AI speaks, admits when it doesn't know, and understands 10 languages.
build: Built a RAG medical assistant with LangChain, Pinecone and Mistral AI over 13,828 passages from four sources: the Gale Encyclopedia of Medicine, OpenStax Pharmacology, MedlinePlus and WHO fact sheets.
Raised retrieval Hit@5 from 56% to 100% (MRR 0.52 → 0.87) on a 16-question evaluation by moving to larger chunks and more sources, adding BM25 hybrid search and a cross-encoder reranker.

Put a safety layer in front of the model: emergency, crisis and dosage rules in English, Hindi and Hinglish, instant 112 / 108 / 14416 helplines, a “won’t guess” relevance cut-off and per-visitor rate limits.
Added 10-language support detected from the script, voice input and spoken answers, and lab-report and photo analysis with values range-checked in code rather than by the LLM.
Developed a Flask app with streaming answers, saved SQLite chat history, feedback review, dark and light themes and an animated landing page.

Containerised it with Docker and set up GitHub Actions CI (103 pytest tests, both images built on every push); a lite mode with ONNX embeddings and a hosted reranker cuts memory from ~2 GB to ~240 MB, so it runs free on Render and redeploys when CI passes.
features: Answers only from trusted medical sources, with the sources listed under every reply
Hybrid search (Pinecone vectors + BM25) with cross-encoder reranking of the top results
Safety layer that spots emergencies, crises and dosage requests before the AI answers
10 languages detected from the script, with voice input and spoken answers
Explains uploaded lab reports and photos, with values range-checked in code
Streaming chat with saved history, feedback, and dark and light themes
Free, containerised deployment with CI on every push

projects.title: CFS Scheduler
projects.logline: How does Linux decide which process runs next? A C++ simulation of the kernel's Completely Fair Scheduler — vruntime, weights and a red-hot runqueue — with every scheduling decision plotted on a timeline.
build: Implemented a simulation of the Linux Completely Fair Scheduler in C++, with weight-based vruntime accounting matching the kernel's NICE_0_LOAD of 1024.
Modelled the runqueue as a min-heap priority queue keyed on vruntime, scheduling the least-served task first.
Simulated CPU-bound and I/O-bound workloads with distinct time-slice and I/O-wait behaviour, measured with std::chrono.
Logged every time slice to CSV and built a Python/Matplotlib Gantt chart to visualise fairness and priority effects.
Structured the project as modular services (process loading, queue, execution, scheduler) built with CMake.
features: Linux-style weights: weight = NICE_0_LOAD (1024) / (priority + 1)
Virtual runtime accounting, so higher-priority tasks age more slowly
Runqueue as a min-heap ordered by vruntime, always picking the fairest task next
Separate CPU-bound (1 ms slice) and I/O-bound (10 ms wait) workload models
Processes loaded from JSON, so new workloads need no recompiling
Gantt-style timeline of every time slice, plotted with Matplotlib

projects.title: SocketChat
projects.logline: A multi-user chat room built from raw TCP sockets in C++ — usernames, timestamps, heartbeat and auto-reconnect — with a browser client through a tiny WebSocket bridge. No libraries.
build: Built a multi-client chat room in C++ on Winsock 2: a thread per client, a shared room guarded by one lock, usernames, timestamps and slash commands.

Designed a length-prefixed wire protocol (4-byte header, 64 KB cap) with control frames and a version handshake, so message boundaries survive TCP and other programs on the port can't pass as the server.

Added a PING/PONG heartbeat (every 5 s, dropped after 15 s of silence) and client auto-reconnect with backoff that rejoins under the same name; replaced blocking calls with short select() polls for reliable shutdown.
Wrote a standard-library Python bridge that serves a browser UI and speaks WebSocket to the room, with an origin check; the UI renders messages as text, never HTML.
Documented the protocol, MinGW and MSVC build steps, security limits and a roadmap.
features: Multi-user room: one thread per client, with every message relayed to everyone
Usernames (duplicates get a suffix), timestamps and /users, /help and /quit commands
Heartbeat every 5 s drops silent clients after 15 s; clients auto-reconnect with backoff and rejoin under the same name
Length-prefixed protocol (4-byte header, 64 KB limit), so message boundaries survive TCP
Browser client through a standard-library-only Python WebSocket bridge, with a live online list and light and dark themes
Exclusive port binding and a handshake, so another program can't hijack the chat; the bridge checks the origin

projects.title: APEX
projects.logline: An AI fitness tracker — snap a meal, get calories and macros. In development: the secure foundation (auth, database and AI gateway) is built, and the tracking features are next.
build: Set up a Next.js 16 and React 19 app in TypeScript with Supabase auth (email, magic link, Google) and a Postgres schema with row-level security on all five tables.
Built an AI gateway on the Vercel AI SDK that routes each task to a Mistral or Gemini model, falls back to the next model on failure, caps usage per user per day and logs every call.
Wrote a security script that checks users cannot read each other’s data, plus 36 Vitest unit tests.
Added GitHub Actions CI (format, lint, type-check, tests and build) and an APEX design system with a style guide.
Status: Stage 1 (foundation) is complete; tracking features such as meal-photo logging come next.
features: AI gateway: one server-side entry point for Mistral and Gemini, falling back to the next model on failure
Per-user daily AI limits, with every call logged
Six AI task routes ready, including meal-photo analysis
Supabase sign-in with email, magic link and Google
Row-level security on all five tables, checked by a security script
